tools.name: status_create_event
tools.description: Create a shareable event invite link where guests RSVP, for a party, dinner, birthday, trip, night out or other get-together; the host can then add a date poll and split costs on the same page. Use when the user is planning something with other people and wants a link to send round. Not for calendar

tools.name: status_get_event
tools.description: Read an event invite made with status_create_event: who is coming and how many people have replied (each guest's name and RSVP: confirmed for yes, maybe, pass for no, or pending), its title, details, place, date, time and theme, and whether the user has claimed it. Needs the eventId and editKey from

tools.name: status_update_event
tools.description: Change the title, details, place, date, time or theme of an event invite made with status_create_event. Send eventId, editKey and only the fields to change. The invite link stays the same and guests see the change straight away. Does not change a date poll, the guest list or costs, and cannot cancel

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: status_create_event · Private data: status_create_event · Public sink: status_create_event, status_update_event · Destructive: status_update_event.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: status_create_event · Private data: status_create_event · Public sink: status_create_event, status_update_event · Destructive: status_update_event

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
